office_does: The three county commissioners are Skagit County's legislative body: they adopt the county budget, set land-use and permitting policy, and run county services such as the Guemes Island ferry.
race_blurb: Appointed Democratic Commissioner Joe Burns faces Republican state Sen. Keith Wagoner, who led the District 3 primary 45% to 40.7%; the whole county votes in the general. With a roughly $10 million deficit ahead, Wagoner runs on cutting spending and opposing tax increases while keeping his Senate seat, and Burns runs as a full-time commissioner focused on affordability and preserving services.

candidates.summary: 39th District state senator and Senate Minority Whip since 2018, former Sedro-Woolley mayor and 23-year Navy and Marine Corps aviator; would keep his Senate seat through January 2029 if elected.
highlights: Voted against the 2026 millionaires' income tax (ESSB 6346) and the 2025 capital gains/estate (ESSB 5813) and services excise (ESSB 5814) tax bills [S13][S15][S17]
Would scour the county budget to cut 'nice-to-have' spending and seek solutions that 'do not involve taking money out of our pockets' [S9][S12]
Wants faster county permitting for housing and fewer regulatory steps for building [S10][S12]
Supports Flock license-plate cameras with regulation; cites FOP Legislator of the Year award and co-responder legislation [S1][S4][S12]
Endorsed by the Skagit County Republican Party [S6]

taxes.basis: Nay votes on ESSB 6346, ESSB 5813 and ESSB 5814, plus repeated statements opposing county tax increases and a platform of revenue-sharing bills framed as property-tax relief.

spending.basis: Says he would reassess and reduce county spending, sorting expenditures into essential, valuable and nice-to-have, and close the deficit without raising taxes.

housing.basis: Emphasizes removing regulatory steps and speeding housing permits; cites cutting taxes on multi-family housing.

safety.basis: Platform stresses standing with law enforcement and supports Flock cameras, though he also sponsored co-responder training legislation.

experience.basis: Runs on long tenure as councilmember, mayor and state senator (Minority Whip) and calls himself the most experienced candidate.

candidates.summary: Appointed District 3 commissioner since January 2026, former Sedro-Woolley council member and high school auto shop teacher, running as a full-time commissioner focused on affordability.
highlights: Would preserve senior center and Meals on Wheels funding and warns against 'extreme cuts' in the 2027 deficit [S11]
Backs streamlined permitting, more housing types and first-time-buyer pathways [S3][S8]
Supported the county's data center moratorium, citing water, power and floodplain concerns [S12][S13][S14]
Now opposes Flock license-plate cameras; emphasizes behavioral health and the North Star initiative [S3][S11][S14]
Voted with the board to uphold 2025 Guemes ferry fares after a court ordered them recalculated [S15]

spending.basis: Would protect discretionary services like senior centers and Meals on Wheels and invest in rural infrastructure, while also citing budget prioritization.

housing.basis: Primary housing remedies are permit streamlining and zoning for more housing types, with a focus on homeownership rather than tenant protections or public housing.

safety.basis: Emphasizes behavioral health, substance-use prevention and overdose response through North Star, and says he will not approve Flock cameras.

experience.basis: Nine-month appointed incumbent with four years on a city council who says he brings new ideas and creativity rather than decades of experience.
